why: Process events in time order with two FIFO queues and a priority rule that depends on what happened in the previous second. Each second, admit arrivals, pick a queue by the rules, serve one person; when both queues are empty, jump time to the next arrival and forget the last direction.
hints: What state decides who goes next? The two queues and the direction used in the previous second (or 'idle').
Loop over seconds: push everyone with arrival <= t, then choose: the only nonempty queue; else the previous direction if the last second was busy; else direction 1.
If both queues are empty, set t to the next arrival and mark the previous second idle, so time never steps through gaps one by one. O(n).
pitfalls: After an idle gap, priority resets to direction 1, even if the last person served went the other way.
Arrivals at second t can be served at second t.
Do not step t one second at a time across gaps of up to 10^9.
